specification.title: Two runners released together against a database with no history storage
steps: Runners A and B each connect and wait at a start barrier. The database has no history storage.
Release both at once. A runner that executes m1 waits at the gate K.
For the bound, each runner may exit, reach the gate, or wait on the framework's own coordination. Then release K and require both to finish within the deadline.
Checkpoint `after-end`, as soon as both runners have returned: the runner records the state at report time.

invariants.statement: After every runner has finished, the migration's marker count is 1 and history holds one entry for it.
A runner that did not apply the migration either waited and then found it applied, or reported failure (non-zero exit status).
No runner starts executing the migration while another runner's execution of it is still live (its session still inside the migration): two live sessions inside it at once is a violation.

execution.description: Positive control: reads the command tag of PostgreSQL's reply to COMMIT, reports a COMMIT error as a failure, and discards a connection whose ROLLBACK failed. It starts a transaction at the isolation level requested of it.

server.version: PostgreSQL 18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2) on aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit

knowledge: Neither runner can see, before it starts, that the other is about to apply the same migration. The database starts with no history row that could tell it so.

api_outcome.basis: history already held an entry, so the control applied nothing
api_outcome.contract: The correct control runs a migration in one transaction. It takes a transaction-scoped advisory lock before it reads history, applies the migration only when history has no entry, and commits the marker and the history entry together. A reversal deletes the marker and the history entry, refuses a migration that has no reversal, and rolls back a reversal that raises.
